title: Functional Surface-immobilization of Genes Using Multistep Strand Displacement Lithography
protocol: Mix water and ammonia solution in a beaker glass.
Heat the mixture to 70 °C on a hot plate while stirring.
Add hydrogen peroxide to the heated mixture.
Submerge the substrate into the heated mixture.
Rinse the substrate thoroughly with water from a wash bottle after 30 min.
Dry the substrate with a nitrogen gun.
Proceed immediately with PEGylation of the substrate.
Dissolve Biotin-PEG-Silane in dry toluene by vortexing (5 mg/mL).
Place the substrate in a glass petri dish (120 cm diameter, 2 cm height) in a fume hood.

Pipette the solution (≈200 µL for a single glass cover slip, a few mL for a large silicon wafer) onto the substrate, covering the whole surface, but avoid the solution flowing over the edge of the substrate.
Close the petri dish.
Add an additional cover with a wet paper towel to reduce drying of the substrate.
After 30 min, add approximately 40 ml of isopropyl alcohol.
Take out the substrate and rinse it again thoroughly with isopropyl alcohol.
Dry the substrate with a nitrogen gun (for glass slides, remember the PEGylated side).
Store the substrate in the dark until use.
Use modified primers to amplify the gene of interest by polymerase chain reaction (PCR).
Purify the DNA using a spin column purification kit.
Measure the concentration of the DNA using an absorption photometer.
The concentration should not be much lower than 100 nM.
Adjust the concentration of NaCl to 1 M using a concentrated 5 M NaCl solution.
Prepare the Bephore-mix (1 µM streptavidin, 1.5 µM PC DNA, 7.5 µM PH DNA in 1x PBS).
Store the Bephore-mix in the dark in the fridge for several weeks.
Prepare the passivation mix (10 µM unlabeled DIS DNA, 1 mg/mL BSA in 1x PBS).
Store the passivation mix in the dark in the fridge for several weeks.
Cut the substrate into smaller pieces using a glass cutter or by breaking along a crystal line with a scalpel.
Create a short scratch from the center towards an edge of the substrate using the glass cutter as an alignment mark.
Blow small particles off the chip with a nitrogen gun.
Mix two droplets of two-component silicone glue and stir with a pipette tip.
Apply the glue to the surface of the chip, leaving the area around the tip of the scratch blank.
Incubate 10 µL of Bephore-mix at room temperature on the chip.
Place the chip in a box partially filled with water to reduce evaporation during incubation.
Wash the chip several times (5x with 50 µL) with 1x PBS after 1 hour.
Incubate 10 µL of passivation-mix on the chip at room temperature.
Wash the chip several times (10x with 50 µL) with 1x PBS after 2 hours.
Place the substrate on a microscopy slide.
Move the microscopy slide to the microscope stage.
Insert black foil between the microscopy slide and Bephore glass slide for patterning.
Insert a red filter into the illumination path.
Focus onto the substrate surface.
Navigate to the region of the substrate to be exposed.
Insert the mask holder, block the illumination, and change to the UV filter.
Open the shutter at low light intensity.
Use the camera to focus the mask on the substrate.
Block the light path to the camera and illuminate the substrate at high light intensity for the desired exposure time.
Take the sample from the microscope.
Carefully remove as much buffer as possible from the substrate without drying it.
Add 10-20 μL of DNA with DIS-sequence to the substrate.
Place the substrate in a wet box to prevent drying.
Incubate the DNA on the substrate for 2 hours at room temperature (for oligonucleotides) or several hours/overnight at room temperature (for longer DNA fragments).
Remove the DNA from the chip.
Wash the chip several times with 1x PBS.
Store and reuse the DNA taken from the substrate to reduce waste.
Clean a silicon wafer by sonication in acetone for 5 min at high power and rinse with isopropyl alcohol and de-ionized water.
Place the wafer on a hot plate at 150 °C for 15 min.
Heat the wafer to 120 °C for 2 min.
Add about 2-3 mL photoresist.
Spin the wafer for 15 s at 500 rpm.
Spin the wafer at 3000 rpm for 30 s.
Let the photoresist layer relax at room temperature for 10 min.
Place the wafer on a hot plate at 50 °C for 2 min.
Place the wafer on a hot plate at 85 °C for 5 min.
Place the wafer under the photomask with the blueprint of the compartments.
Expose the wafer for 1 min with UV-light through the photomask.
Place the wafer at 50 °C for 2 min after exposure.
Place the wafer at 85 °C for 5 min after exposure.
Let the wafer cool down and relax for 1 h at room temperature.
Place the wafer in a dish with developer for 3 min while gently agitating the beaker.
Rinse the wafer with isopropyl alcohol.
Dry the wafer with a nitrogen gun.
Place the wafer on a hot plate at 130 °C for 45 min.
Mix PDMS base and PDMS curing agent in a 10:1 ratio.
Pour the mixture onto the wafer in a closed container until a layer of about 5 mm has formed above the wafer.
Apply a vacuum (about 85 kPa) to the container for about 30 min.
Heat the PDMS to about 70°C for 1-2 h in an oven.
Separate the PDMS device from the wafer.
Cut the PDMS into slabs so that each piece contains one set of compartments.
Punch holes (1 mm diameter) as an inlet and outlet at the ends of the supply channel if connected to a microfluidic setup.
Clean the PDMS with isopropyl alcohol and de-ionized water.
Dry the PDMS with a nitrogen gun.
Store the PDMS dust-free.
Prepare a Bephore chip with alignment mark using double-sided adhesive tape on the chip holder.
Immobilize one or multiple genes on the chip.
Add some vacuum grease around the central hole of the bottom holder.
Plug in the chip holder.
Prepare a thin PDMS chip with compartments using the spin coating procedure in step 4.2.1.
Cut the PDMS as small as possible, leaving a channel open to one side for waste and precursor molecule exchange by diffusion.
Clean a glass cover slip (24 mm x 24 mm, no. 1.5) and the backside of the PDMS chip with oxygen plasma for 42 s.
Place the PDMS chip at the center of the glass slide with the compartments pointing upwards.
Bake the glass with the PDMS for 1 h at 70 °C.
Add some vacuum grease around the large hole of the top holder.
Clean the glass slide and the PDMS chip with oxygen plasma for 42 s before starting the experiment to render the PDMS hydrophilic.
Place the glass slide with the PDMS onto the top holder.
Gently press the glass onto the grease.
Remove buffer from the chip.
Wash the chip once with 10 µL of cell-free expression system.
Add 60 µL of cell-free expression system onto the chip.
Remove two-component silicone glue from the edges of the chip.
Add 20 µL of expression system onto the PDMS.
Place droplet onto the PDMS and check under a stereoscopic microscope for air bubbles.
Wash off any air bubbles with the rest of the cell-free expression system.
Immobilize the bottom holder with a gripper arm.
Insert the top holder into the bottom holder.
Lower the top holder until the cell-free expression system droplets fuse.
Check through the stereoscopic microscope whether compartments and alignment mark are in similar regions.
Re-position the glass slide on the top holder if necessary.
Screw up the wingnuts from the bottom until they touch the bottom side of the holder.
Tighten the wingnuts gently while aligning the compartments and chip via the handle at the bottom.
Spray the sponge in the anti-evaporation enclosure with water and insert the holder into the box.
Fill a 5 mL syringe with two-component silicone glue and use it to seal the box.
Transfer the box to a temperature-controlled microscope.
Image the DNA brush and the reaction in fluorescence microscopy.
Prepare the cell-free expression system in a sample tube containing about 200 μL.
Add polystyrene beads labeled with fluorescent dyes to monitor flow rate through the supply channel.
Connect the sample tube to a pressure controller.
Place the connected tube in an ice reservoir and keep cold for approximately 12 hours, refilling ice as necessary.
Alternatively, connect the tube to a syringe pump for constant flow rate control over long-term experiments.
Attach PTFE tubing (inner diameter of 0.8 mm) to the tube containing the cell-free expression system.
Insert a broken syringe needle piece with blunt ends into the PTFE tubing for later connection to PDMS.
Wrap the PTFE tubing around larger rubber tubing connected to an ice water reservoir and peristaltic pump, securing them with Scotch tape.
Clean the flat side of the PDMS chip using oxygen plasma treatment for 42 seconds.
Place the treated PDMS chip on a microscopy slide with holes fitting the inlet and outlet of the PDMS.
Ensure that micro-chambers are not facing the glass slide during placement.
Apply double-sided adhesive tape to the flat side of the PDMS holder.
Stick a piece of black foil in the region between the two holes of the holder.
Stick the glass slide with the PDMS chip to the holder.
Treat the PDMS and the PDMS holder with oxygen plasma for 42 seconds.
Apply vacuum grease around the large hole in the top holder.
Insert the PDMS holder into the top holder.
Connect PTFE tubing with a syringe needle connector to the inlet of the PDMS chip.
Insert a second piece of PTFE tubing (about 5 cm) with a syringe needle connector at the outlet.
Position the PDMS holder in the top holder so it can move freely in all directions.
Place the top holder loosely onto the heated stage without tightening any wingnuts.
Navigate to the position of the PDMS compartments using the microscope and center them in the camera's field of view.
Set the temperature of the heated stage to 37 °C.
Glue a Bephore glass slide with the gene brushes to the temperature-controlled stage of the inverted fluorescence microscope using double-sided adhesive tape.
Position the alignment mark approximately at the center of the microscope's field of view.
Take an image in the corresponding fluorescence channel of the gene brush and mark its position in the camera image.
Remove the buffer from the gene brush, ensuring it does not dry out.
Add 20 µL of the cell-free expression system to the gene brush.
Use tweezers to remove the silicone glue frame.
Pressure-fill the PTFE tubing with the cell-free expression system until it appears at the bottom of the PDMS device.
Pipette 10 µL of cell-free expression system onto the micro-chambers on the PDMS.
Ensure the compartments are free of air bubbles.
Carefully lower the top holder onto the glass slide and align the micro-chambers with the gene brush.
Precisely align the x-y-position and orientation of the PDMS device with the gene brush using the small screws at the back of the PDMS holder.
Hold the position and press the PDMS onto the glass slide by tightening the wingnuts along the screws that connect the top holder to the microscope stage.
Increase the pressure in the tube containing the cell-free expression system.
Monitor the flow of the fluorescent beads through the supply channel (flow rates between 0.5 to 5 µl per hour are recommended).
If necessary, increase the pressure of the PDMS on the glass by tightening the wingnuts.
